title: CTAB DNA Extraction of High Polysaccharide Samples
author: Mai-Britt Mosbech
materials: Let the tube cool to RT.

steps.title: Prepare frozen ground tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.2–1 g of frozen ground sample tissue to a tube and immediately shake, invert and vortex to mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Perform sorbitol wash
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL sorbitol wash buffer to a 50 mL tube, add 1 200 µL β‑mercaptoethanol (BME), and mix.

steps.title: Add BME and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add BME and Proteinase K to individual tubes containing CTAB lysis buffer and pre‑heat the mixture to 65 °C.

steps.title: Add pre‑warmed CTAB lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the pre‑warmed CTAB lysis buffer to the sorbitol‑washed pellet and vortex for ~5 seconds to obtain a homogeneous suspension.

steps.title: Incubate at 65 °C with agitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 65 °C for at least 1 hour with agitation at 800 rpm.

steps.title: Add chloroform:isoamyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1 volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1) and vortex/shake until the phases are thoroughly mixed.

steps.title: Centrifuge to separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 °C for 10 minutes at 4 700 × g with acceleration 9 and deceleration 6.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Gently transfer the aqueous (upper) phase to a new tube. If clumps appear near the interphase, break up the DNA by pipetting or vortexing before a second chloroform rinse.

steps.title: Optional high‑yield CTAB addition
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL pre‑warmed CTAB lysis buffer to the organic phase, repeat the chloroform extraction, and combine the new aqueous phase with the previous one.

steps.title: Optional high‑purity repeat
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 6–8 (chloroform extraction and aqueous‑phase collection) for higher purity; if step 9 was performed, use less than 1 × volume of CTAB buffer.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 0.6–0.7 volume of room‑temperature isopropanol to the combined aqueous phase and gently invert the tube 10 times.

steps.title: Incubate for DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at room temperature for at least 15 minutes to allow DNA precipitation.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 °C for 30 minutes at 4 700 × g.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant (or pipette it out for 2 mL tubes) without disturbing the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash pellet
steps.instruction: Add freshly prepared 70 % ethanol, gently swirl and invert the tube, then let the pellet soak for 15 minutes at room temperature (or rotate at 10–20 rpm).

steps.title: Centrifuge after ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 °C for 10 minutes at 4 700 × g.

steps.title: Transfer pellet to smaller tube (optional)
steps.instruction: If desired, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, transfer the pellet to a 1.5 mL tube using a wide‑bore p1000 tip, and decant the supernatant.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol‑wash, centrifugation, and decant steps at least once; if isopropanol precipitation was used, consider a third ethanol wash to remove excess salt.

steps.title: Final ethanol removal and spin
steps.instruction: After the last wash, carefully decant the supernatant, then centrifuge at 4 700 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Quick spin to remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Perform a brief spin to gather residual ethanol at the tube bottom and remove it with a P20 tip; repeat if necessary.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 5–15 minutes (≈10 minutes) at room temperature, taking care not to overdry.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in buffer
steps.instruction: Add resuspension buffer (Elution Buffer, low‑TE, or TE) and mix gently overnight at room temperature; no pipetting. Alternatively, incubate 3–4 days at 4 °C/RT or a short 50 °C incubation to aid resuspension.

steps.title: Conditional repeat sorbitol wash
steps.instruction: If the supernatant after resuspension is turbid, viscous, or darkly colored, repeat the sorbitol wash.
